No observable behavior change to any command: the only production-file edits authorised are wording -- core.die's docstring (task 4), the restrict_agent_ingress log line (task 5) and the STATIC_MANIFESTS description (task 7). Every guard this sweep adds must be a COMMITTED assertion that a normal green pytest run exercises, AND must itself be pinned by a committed negative test proving it bites. Handoff-only evidence -- 'run the mutation and report the output' -- NEVER satisfies an acceptance criterion: it does not survive into the graded diff, so the evaluator cannot check it and a later reader cannot rely on it. No mutation of a real repo file is ever committed. No skips, no xfail, no relaxed existing assertion, no lint suppression, and no test deleted or weakened to make room.

tasks.title: Stop the -O child tests from inheriting the operator's real credentials and .env
tasks.why: A plain pytest run is one refactor of main()'s first two lines away from a paid model turn and a live ClickHouse Cloud query against the operator's own cluster.
tasks.notes: From security finding sec2 of improve-merge-cycle-cleanup. READ IT FIRST. Neither -O test requests the `redirected` fixture, so the child gets the developer's full environment and a live core.ROOT, and one of them calls smoke.main(['--target','eks']). CORRECTION TO THE FINDING'S REMEDIATION, verified this cycle: its second half suggests pointing the child at a redirected root 'by inserting a tmp_path on its sys.path instead of the live core.ROOT'. That CANNOT work -- core.ROOT is derived from __file__ (launcher/core.py:12), so the child recomputes the live checkout no matter what sys.path holds, and the child must keep the real root on sys.path to import scripts.smoke at all. Override core.ROOT inside the child's own program text instead, the way the `redirected` fixture does in-process at tests/conftest.py:303-304. require_assertions() is main()'s second line (scripts/smoke.py:537, after parse_args), so it still fires before any .env read -- the root override is defense in depth for the case where that ordering regresses, not a replacement for it.

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes

optimised() hands the child an environment with every conftest.REDIRECT_KEYS entry removed -- the 21-key union that holds API_KEY, the five CLICKHOUSE_*/OTLP keys and the six LANGFUSE_* keys -- while keeping whatever the interpreter needs to start (PATH, HOME, and PYTHONPATH if set). Passed via core.run(..., env=...), which forwards **kwargs to subprocess.run.

The child cannot read the operator's real root .env: its program overrides core.ROOT (and core.RUNTIME) to a throwaway directory before importing anything that calls config.load_env(). Implemented in the child's program text, not via sys.path -- see the task notes.

Both existing -O tests still assert what they asserted before, including the control assert that proves the child really was optimised (tests/test_smoke_queries.py:280,286). The scrub must not make either test vacuous: if the refusal under test can no longer be reached because the environment is empty rather than because the guard fired, the test has stopped testing the guard.
The scrubbed key set is derived from conftest.REDIRECT_KEYS by reference, not re-listed in this file, so a key added to the union is covered here without a second edit.

A COMMITTED regression test sets a sentinel API_KEY in the parent environment, invokes optimised() with a child program that reports os.environ, core.ROOT and core.RUNTIME, and asserts the sentinel is absent, core.ROOT is not the repository root, and core.RUNTIME is under the redirected root. The test must fail if either the env scrub or the root/runtime override is removed.

tasks.title: Replace the unsound AWS env isolation in use_profile with the save/restore shape
tasks.why: use_profile uses the exact mechanism task 8 of the prior cycle proved unsound and replaced, and its docstring makes a restoration claim that is false on the machine the test parametrizes for.
tasks.notes: From quality finding q1 of improve-merge-cycle-cleanup -- the sharpest finding of that cycle. READ IT FIRST. monkeypatch.delenv records no undo entry for an already-absent key, so on a machine with AWS_REGION unset (bare CI -- the case the profile-unset parameter exists to cover) the AWS_REGION that aws.aws_login() writes directly at launcher/eks/aws.py:38 outlives the test. Nothing reddens today ONLY because the prior cycle's REDIRECT_KEYS union happens to include AWS_REGION -- a sibling task's scrub containing this task's leak. Two routes are acceptable (finding's own remediation): the save/restore shape from tests/conftest.py:305-313, or converting the two guard tests to request the shared `redirected` fixture with AWS_PROFILE supplied through a redirect_env override. If you take the second route, mind the teardown-ordering trap that tests/test_conftest.py:70-78 documents: the setter must be set up BEFORE redirected.

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes

use_profile no longer relies on monkeypatch.delenv for AWS_PROFILE or AWS_REGION. Whatever the caller's shell held before the test is what os.environ holds after it, in both the profile-set and profile-unset parametrizations, including the AWS_REGION that aws_login() exports mid-test.

A COMMITTED test pins the restoration itself: with AWS_REGION absent from the environment, running the guard test leaves AWS_REGION absent afterwards. The prior cycle's equivalent lives at tests/test_conftest.py -- put this beside it or in the same file, but it must be an assertion in the committed suite, not something demonstrated during the session.

The use_profile docstring's restoration claim matches what the code now does. It currently says 'Both keys are handed to monkeypatch even when they are being cleared, so the original values are restored afterwards', which is the false half.
Both existing parametrizations of test_the_dispatch_guard_names_the_subcommand_that_reaches_a_process still exercise the per-invocation no-process guard and still fail if that guard is removed.

tasks.title: Route the node child through core.run so the single-subprocess-importer claim is true again
tasks.why: launcher/core.py:3 states it is the only module that imports subprocess; a sibling task in the prior cycle made that literally false repo-wide.
tasks.notes: From quality finding q2 of improve-merge-cycle-cleanup. READ IT FIRST. Two tasks in the prior cycle each needed to spawn a child from a test and chose different spellings: wave-1 task 4 set the in-cycle precedent by routing its python -O child through core.run with core.PIPE (tests/test_smoke_queries.py:275), and wave-2 task 6 imported subprocess directly in a separate worktree (tests/test_frontend_overlay.py:13, used at :324). The finding offers two routes -- converge on core.run, or amend the core.py docstring to say 'the only module in launcher/'. TAKE THE FIRST: the constraint is load-bearing for how this repo's process surface is faked in one place, and weakening the claim to match the one divergence is the wrong direction for a public reference implementation. Note the test does not use fake_sh, so core.run is unpatched there and the call goes through unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes

tests/test_frontend_overlay.py no longer imports subprocess, and its node child goes through core.run(NODE, '-e', program, stdout=core.PIPE, stderr=core.PIPE, text=True, check=True) or the equivalent, matching the spelling at tests/test_smoke_queries.py:275.

The claim at launcher/core.py:3 holds repo-wide again: `import subprocess` and `from subprocess import ...` appear in launcher/core.py and nowhere else under launcher/, scripts/, tests/ or concierge/. This is a condition on the merged tree, verifiable by the evaluator's own scan -- task 4 is the one that lands the committed guard pinning it (task 4 ac3), which is why task 4 depends on this task.

emitted_env_script(values) at tests/test_frontend_overlay.py:300 returns the same (script, env) 2-tuple it returned before -- that is the function holding the node child at :324, NOT env_script_source() at :276, which is pure regex extraction over the patch text, returns a 3-tuple and spawns nothing. The assertions in test_every_window_env_value_is_a_json_literal_not_a_quoted_interpolation and its two siblings are unchanged in meaning, and check=True still surfaces a node failure as a failure rather than a confusing KeyError on stdout.
launcher/core.py is NOT edited by this task. The claim is restored by fixing the violation, not by narrowing the claim.

A committed guard pins constraint 1 -- the claim at launcher/core.py:3 that core.py is the only module importing subprocess. Factor the AST scan into a module-level helper, then assert over launcher/, scripts/, tests/ and concierge/ that `import subprocess` and `from subprocess import ...` appear in launcher/core.py alone, with a failure message naming every offending file. tasks.notes: From security finding sec1 AND quality finding q3 of improve-merge-cycle-cleanup -- one task because both are conditions under the same protection and both guards land in tests/test_eks_check.py. READ BOTH FIRST. sec1: enableNetworkPolicy appears in five places repo-wide (README.md:148, launcher/eks/lifecycle.py:150, deploy/eks/k8s/network-policy.yaml:23, deploy/eks/README.md:78 and :130) and in exactly one code site, deploy/eks/tofu/eks.tf:67 -- asserted zero times. tofu validate does not check add-on configuration_values payloads. q3: the selector guard reads the agent and frontend pod labels out of the committed recordings, and both recordings carry helm.sh/chart: opentelemetry-demo-0.41.0 (langfuse-configured.yaml:449,583; langfuse-not-configured.yaml:444,578,685), matching config.CHART_VERSION at launcher/eks/config.py:19. SCOPE BOUNDARY: this task READS deploy/eks/tofu/eks.tf and must not modify it -- see constraint 2. The prior cycle's single Tofu authorisation is spent. On sec1's optional second half: do NOT add the `aws eks describe-addon` call. It puts a live AWS round-trip in a deploy path for a claim the docstring already documents; fix the log's unconditional wording instead (ac4).

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes

A committed test reads deploy/eks/tofu/eks.tf and asserts the vpc-cni add-on's configuration_values payload carries enableNetworkPolicy = "true". A regex over the file text is sufficient; no HCL parser. The failure message names deploy/eks/k8s/network-policy.yaml as the thing this setting makes real, so an editor who drops it learns what they switched off.

A committed assertion pins both recordings to the chart pin: for each of langfuse-configured.yaml and langfuse-not-configured.yaml, f'opentelemetry-demo-{config.CHART_VERSION}' appears as a helm.sh/chart label. The failure message tells the editor to re-run the regeneration command in the fixture header, so a CHART_VERSION bump cannot leave the selector guard passing against a stale label set.

launcher/eks/lifecycle.py:154 no longer reports a restriction unconditionally. Its log line names the add-on dependency (or is otherwise phrased so an operator on a cluster applied before enableNetworkPolicy went in is not told ingress was restricted when nothing is filtering). No new process call, no behavior change to what gets applied.

Both new guards are themselves guarded by COMMITTED negative tests. Factor each assertion's decision into a helper taking text rather than reading the file inline -- one over the eks.tf text, one over a recording's chart labels -- and commit a test for each that feeds it the failing input (eks.tf text with the enableNetworkPolicy line absent; a recording whose helm.sh/chart label names a version other than config.CHART_VERSION) and asserts the guard reports the problem and names it. No mutation of a real repo file is committed, and the real files stay as they are.
deploy/eks/tofu/ is unmodified. Confirm with git diff --stat that no file under that directory appears in this task's diff.
The existing test_the_agent_network_policy_selects_the_pods_the_chart_actually_renders keeps its current assertions; the new guards sit beside it rather than replacing any part of it.

tasks.why: The prior cycle's consolidation moved half the argparse internals and told readers they live in one place, and the cycle's four pinned inventories fail tests in files the editor is not touching with nothing to discover them from.
tasks.notes: From quality findings q4 and q6 of improve-merge-cycle-cleanup. READ BOTH FIRST. q4: task 8 absorbed the _SubParsersAction lookup into conftest.subparsers_action (tests/conftest.py:316), but names_rather_than_runs at tests/test_docs.py:161 still walks parser._actions and reads option_strings/nargs itself -- so the consolidation's own justification ('an upgrade that moves them breaks one line rather than one per test module', conftest.py:319-320) is only partly delivered. q6 is severity info and its own remediation says it is not worth a code change on its own; it is here because this task is already the one editing conftest.py. RUNS AFTER TASKS 4 AND 5 BY DESIGN: task 4 widens the refusal guard's scope to scripts/ and task 5 adds a chart-pin guard, so an index written against the current tree would be stale at merge. Read what those tasks actually landed before writing the list -- this is the whole reason for the dependency. CODEX ROUND 1 (f2) CAUGHT A MISSED EDGE: task 7 also lands a mechanical inventory -- a committed equality guard between config.STATIC_MANIFESTS and the manifests the deploy path actually applies -- so an index written without it would have its critical ac4 false after consolidation. acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes

tasks.title: Make the STATIC_MANIFESTS contract true, or stop claiming it
tasks.why: config.STATIC_MANIFESTS is documented as every manifest applied unchanged and eks check iterates it, but the deploy path applies the two individually -- so a third entry would be parsed by the check and never applied to the cluster.
tasks.notes: NOT a debt item -- this is a latent bug the prior cycle's quality reviewer surfaced OUTSIDE its findings, so it carries no finding id. VERIFIED THIS CYCLE: launcher/eks/config.py:84-86 documents STATIC_MANIFESTS as 'Every manifest under k8s_dir() that is applied unchanged'; launcher/eks/check.py:129 iterates the tuple; but the deploy path applies each one individually in two different functions -- restrict_agent_ingress at launcher/eks/lifecycle.py:154 and deploy_collector at :167. Add a third entry and eks check validates it while eks deploy never applies it. DO NOT collapse the two applies into a loop: they are deliberately ordered and separately post-processed (the policy goes in before the release exists, the collector is applied then waited on then tailed), and lifecycle.py is task 5's file this wave -- see constraint 6. The fix is a guard that the tuple and the applied set cannot silently disagree, plus honest wording. tests/test_eks_deploy.py already records the deploy's process sequence via fake_sh and the Recorder/Steps shape, which is where the applied set can be read.

acceptance_criteria.text: The full verification command passes

A committed test asserts that every config.STATIC_MANIFESTS entry is actually applied by a full eks deploy run, read from the recorded kubectl apply calls rather than from a hand-kept list. Adding a third entry to the tuple must fail this test until the deploy path applies it.

The guard is itself guarded by a COMMITTED negative test: with config.STATIC_MANIFESTS monkeypatched to carry a third manifest name that the deploy path does not apply, the collection logic reports that third name as unapplied. Assert on the reported name, so the test fails if the guard goes silent rather than merely if it changes shape. No edit to the real tuple is committed.
launcher/eks/config.py:84-86's description of STATIC_MANIFESTS states the relationship that now actually holds between the tuple, eks check and the deploy path.
launcher/eks/lifecycle.py is NOT edited, and the two applies keep their current order and their separate post-processing. The deploy's observable behavior is unchanged: same processes, same sequence.

config.STATIC_MANIFESTS, config.COLLECTOR_MANIFEST and config.NETWORK_POLICY_MANIFEST keep their names and values -- tests/test_eks_check.py:485,505-508 read them and that file belongs to task 5 this wave.

The only edit to launcher/eks/config.py is the STATIC_MANIFESTS description at :84-86. CHART_VERSION at :19 is untouched -- task 5 pins the render recordings to its value this wave, and launcher/eks/check.py, k8s.py, lifecycle.py and three other test modules read it.

plan_review_findings.recommendation: Add a critical AC requiring a committed regression test that injects a sentinel credential into the parent and directly verifies both isolation limbs in the child.

suggested_change.proposed: {"id":"ac6","text":"A COMMITTED regression test sets a sentinel API_KEY in the parent environment, invokes optimised() with a child program that reports os.environ, core.ROOT and core.RUNTIME, and asserts the sentinel is absent, core.ROOT is not the repository root, and core.RUNTIME is under the redirected root. log.note: Phase 4.5 conflict analysis, all four classes, run against 629f6cb. LEXICAL: 9 predicted files across the 6 wave-1 tasks, all unique -- no file is claimed twice anywhere in the plan. SYMBOLIC (the class I missed last cycle, which blocked task 3 there): grepped 16 cross-task identifiers. Five real edges found and all are pinned from BOTH sides rather than left to luck -- (a) config.STATIC_MANIFESTS is edited by task 7 and read by task 5's tests/test_eks_check.py:485,505-508, pinned by task 7 ac6 and constraint 7; (b) config.CHART_VERSION is DEFINED in task 7's file at :19 and read by task 5's new chart pin, pinned by task 7's new ac7 confining its config.py edit to :84-86; (c) core.die is edited by task 4 and called by 15 launcher modules plus scripts/smoke.py, pinned by task 4's new ac6 confining its core.py edit to the docstring; (d) launcher/core.py's module docstring is the claim task 3 restores, so ac6 also forbids task 4 from editing it -- the claim is restored by fixing the violation, not by narrowing the text; (e) conftest.REDIRECT_KEYS is newly read by task 1 and its file is edited by task 6, pinned by task 6 ac6 and separated by wave. SHARED INFRASTRUCTURE: none -- no task touches deploy/, docker/, .env.example or a CI file, and constraint 2 forbids the Tofu tree outright. TEST INTERFERENCE: one candidate edge checked and CLEARED -- task 5 rewords the restrict_agent_ingress log line and task 7's guard runs a full eks deploy in tests/test_eks_deploy.py, so an exact-output assertion there would break at merge; verified nothing in tests/ or launcher/ asserts that log text, and test_eks_deploy.py's capsys assertions at :544-560 are substring-based on tunnel URLs. WAVE LAYOUT: task 6 is alone in wave 2 and depends on 4 and 5 for a SEMANTIC reason, not a lexical one -- its q6 deliverable is an index of the suite's mechanical guards, and tasks 4 and 5 both change what those guards pin (widened refusal scope, new chart pin), so an index written against the current tree would be stale the moment wave 1 merges.

DEFERRAL LEDGER REPAIR, done while authoring this plan and prompted by Codex round-2 f3. The prior cycle closed its ledger WITHOUT flipping the deferrals its own tasks had resolved: feat-merge-ch-otel-demo.json still carried 19 entries when 15 were done, and feat-otel-demo-eks.json carried d13 whose subject files no longer exist. Left alone this would have inverted the next intake - 15 finished items resurfacing while the 4 real ones sat in the same undifferentiated list. Each of the 15 was verified AGAINST THE CODE rather than against a matching task title before flipping (d1: stack.py:100-102 now calls langfuse_auth_header; d20: require_trace_id refuses via core.die and main refuses under -O; d25: the AST guard pins core.py as the only message site; d27: values.py's redundant gate is gone and image_overrides names require_published as the gate; d28: cluster_reachable only in infra.py and ASSISTANT_PATH only in collector.py; d29: no user-facing hint says scripts/demo.py, the six remaining occurrences are legitimate), and each flip names its resolving task and plan. d13 was dropped as moot. Four entries genuinely remain carried and all four are named in this plan's context as deliberately out of scope: d2, d3, d16 and info-level d21. NOTE FOR THE NEXT CYCLE: this is a harness-level lesson, not a repo one - principle 13 says nothing is dispositioned by forgetting, and a sweep plan's CLOSED ledger stops the sweep emitting NEW deferrals but does nothing to close the SOURCE plan's entries that the sweep's tasks resolved. That flip is the orchestrator's job at sweep close-out and I did not do it last cycle.

CODEX PLAN REVIEW, 2 rounds, 9 findings, ALL 9 APPLIED, 0 deferred, 0 rejected (895s total; round 1 415s, round 2 480s, both at --timeout 900 after last cycle's 482s overrun of the 480s default). Round 1 found six: one AC naming the wrong function and return shape (pr1 - ac4 named env_script_source, which does pure regex extraction and spawns nothing, instead of emitted_env_script, which holds the node child), one missed dependency edge (pr2 - task 7 lands a mechanical inventory too, so task 6's index would have been false after consolidation), and FOUR HANDOFF-ONLY CRITICAL ACs (pr3-pr6). That last group is the same defect I made four times in the prior cycle, except worse: I wrote a constraint forbidding it and then made the probes critical ACs anyway. Resolved by CONVERTING rather than demoting - every probe became a committed negative test - which is a net gain, since plan constraint 1 (subprocess only in launcher/core.py) had zero machine enforcement before this review and now has a committed guard in task 4 ac7. Round 2 found the SAME RULE APPLIED UNEVENLY TWICE MORE: task 1's env scrub and root override had nothing committed that fails when they disappear (pr7), and task 4's ac7 - the guard I added in round 1 - required only a real-tree assertion with no synthetic negative (pr8). Plus pr9 on an incomplete out-of-scope list, which led to the ledger repair logged above. The pattern across both rounds is one thing: I state a rule, apply it where I am looking, and miss the places I am not. Both rounds paid for themselves.
